samples.summary: Indent is refused for the whole subtree when *any* descendant is at MAX_LIST_LEVEL, so Tab/Cmd+] silently no-ops on an item that has room
samples.evidence: `if (delta > 0 && deepest >= MAX_LIST_LEVEL) continue;` uses `subtreeOf(...).deepest`, the deepest level anywhere in the following contiguous deeper run. A list with one level-8 item nested under a level-0 parent (reachable by repeated indents) now makes Tab on the parent — and on every ancestor of the deep item — do nothing at all. The previous per-block code (`if (currentLevel >= MAX_LIST_LEVEL) return;` in editor.ts/text-editor.ts) still indented every item that had room. The behaviour is documented as deliberate in the surrounding comment, but it is a user-visible regression: the gesture produces no feedback and no change.

samples.summary: `isPaintableImageSize`'s new upper bound drops an oversized image entirely (rather than clamping), losing content that previously rendered
samples.evidence: `isPaintableImageSize` returns false for `width > MAX_IMAGE_SIZE || height > MAX_IMAGE_SIZE` (20000 px), and all three call sites — crdt-tree.ts:97, yorkie-doc-store.ts:217, clipboard.ts:132 — then omit `style.image` altogether while keeping the inline's U+FFFC placeholder text. An image whose stored size exceeds the ceiling (e.g. a DOCX `<w:drawing>` EMU extent converted at docx-importer.ts:215-221, which is not clamped on import) therefore disappears from the rendered document, and because the reader materialises the in-memory model *without* it, any subsequent local write of that block persists the loss. Clamping (as every other band in this module does for a finite over-ceiling value) would render large instead of vanishing.

samples.summary: Line heights themselves are still unbanded at layout, so a non-finite font size / line-height multiplier from an in-memory producer still poisons `currentY` for the whole document; table-layout step 5d only repairs row heights
samples.evidence: `assignLineHeights` computes `const lineHeightMultiplier = Math.max(1, resolved.lineHeight);` — `Math.max(1, NaN)` is `NaN` — and `lineHeight = lineHeightMultiplier * maxFontSize`, with `maxFontSize` taken from `style.fontSize` unguarded. The new bands only cover values arriving through the CRDT readers and the paste sanitizer; `packages/docs/src/import/docx-style-map.ts:50` does `style.fontSize = halfPointsToPoints(parseInt(val, 10))`, which is `NaN` for a malformed `w:sz`. For a body paragraph that NaN height makes `currentY + line.height > contentHeight` false forever in `paginateLayout`, so `currentY` goes NaN and every later line is placed at NaN — the exact 'blanks the document for every reader' failure the change cites. Inside a table, step 5d (`table-layout.ts:318-322`) repairs `rowHeights[r]` but leaves `cells[r][c].height` non-finite, so `table-renderer.ts:59/61` still computes a NaN/-Infinity `textYOffset`.
searchedFor: grep Number.isFinite in view/layout.ts and table-layout.ts

samples.summary: A NaN row height emits zero fragments — the row is silently dropped from pagination while the layout still reserves its height
samples.evidence: `while (consumed < rowHeight)` is false immediately when `rowHeight` is `NaN` (and the preceding `if (currentY + rowHeight <= contentHeight)` fast path is also false), so no `PageLine` is pushed for that row at all: it renders nowhere, yet `LayoutTable.totalHeight`/`rowYOffsets` still account for it, so every later row's hit-test geometry is offset from what was painted. The new `MAX_ROW_PAGE_SPAN` bound and the `!(fragHeight > 0)` floor both sit *inside* the loop and cannot help. `computeTableLayout` step 5d makes this unreachable for layouts it builds, but `paginateLayout` takes any `DocumentLayout` (the CLI paginator and tests construct `LayoutTable`s directly), so the guard is on the producer rather than on the consumer the change set out to make self-bounding.
